name: ottolenghi sweet potato galette
instructions:
The minimal sweet potato galette in the Ottolenghi style (split from the former sweet-potato-pies-and-galettes house): sweet potato + onion + garlic on a thin layer of sour cream or crème fraîche, dill + aleppo pepper as the drivers, no gravy anywhere. Crust: [[atk-galette-dough]] (whole wheat, white vinegar).

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. SAUTÉ the onions and garlic.
2. BRAISE the sweet potato in CHICKEN STOCK until soft — then DISCARD the stock (flavoring medium, not a gravy; cool the vegetables in the stock before draining to maximize absorption).
3. SPREAD a thin layer of sour cream or crème fraîche on the rolled-out crust — under the vegetables, the way Ottolenghi does.
4. Top with the vegetables; season with DRIED DILL, ALEPPO PEPPER, and LEMON JUICE (no zest).
5. Fold the galette. BAKE AT 400°F to quickly settle the dough; take it out MIDWAY to add the EGG WASH, then keep going at 400°F.
notes:
=== THE SETTLED DECISIONS ===

- MUSHROOMS, CHARD, AND TURNIPS ARE OUT. (Mushrooms: no room, and they're in too many savory pies already — not clashing, just not here. Chard and turnips live in [[sweet-potato-turnip-pie]].)
- GREEK YOGURT DOESN'T WORK — it WEEPS AND CURDLES in the bake. The binder is a THIN LAYER OF SOUR CREAM OR CRÈME FRAÎCHE ON THE BOTTOM of the galette — under the vegetables, not mixed through them.
- DILL + ALEPPO PEPPER ARE THE DRIVERS. Aleppo confirmed by experiment — in the filling before the oven, it does a lot. (Fresno judged too sweet against sweet potato; fresh serrano baked on top is the Ottolenghi-faithful alternative.)
- LEMON JUICE, NO ZEST.
- THE BRAISE-AND-DISCARD STOCK MOVE: braise the sweet potato in chicken stock, discard it. Salt + glutamate diffuse into the vegetable (oden/daikon logic); cooling the vegetables IN the liquid before draining is where most of the absorption happens. The exchange runs both ways — some vegetable flavor leaves with the discarded stock; that's the price of no-gravy.

=== BAKE (PROVEN) — 400°F, EGG WASH MIDWAY ===

Bake at 400°F to quickly settle the galette dough, take it out and add the egg wash midway through, then keep going at 400°F. (Related [[artisan-french-bread]] lesson: glazes applied from the start cause undercooking; midway application sidesteps it. Note the [[apple-pie]] counter-lesson: covered-first fails for raw pastry — the galette never covers, so no conflict.)

=== CRUST-SQUARES FORMAT (OTTOLENGHI OBSERVATIONS) ===

Some people just put the filling on top of SIMPLE CRUST SQUARES rather than making the full folded basin. If doing this approach, OMIT OR USE LESS OF THE ONION.

=== THE CLEANEST VERSION (HYPOTHESIS) ===

Nothing proven yet, but the cleanest form is probably SWEET POTATO + ONION + DILL + ALEPPO PEPPER + CRÈME FRAÎCHE.

=== WANT TO TRY ===

- SAGE — a common pairing in the ottolenghi-style galettes.
- FETA / GOAT CHEESE CRUMBLES and WALNUTS / CHESTNUTS.
- PORK VARIANT: PROCESSED PORK probably best, minced pork shoulder could work. With crème fraîche + onion this is essentially flammkuchen logic — crème fraîche is also the more bake-stable binder against rendering pork fat.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[sweet-potato-turnip-pie]]: the other half of the split — the ATK gravy pie (turnips + chard + mushrooms live there).
- [[atk-galette-dough]]: the crust.
- [[mushroom-leek-galette]]: the other galette.
- [[southern-chickpea-soup]]: the other chicken-stock-as-flavoring-medium dish (there the stock stays; here it's discarded).
- [[ottolenghi-cherry-tomatoes]]: the other Ottolenghi vegetable dish (same chili-and-dairy logic, urfa/aleppo family).
